name: Oral irrigators/water flossers and tips (if included)
anchor: sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant schedules with the Germany BVL 2017 TOOTHPASTE tier as the oral-mucosal anchor for formulated products, and Canada SOR/2018-83's mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling as the article anchor
native_basis: oral-care article as placed on market (total content per accessible part, ug/kg)
native_basis_label: oral-care article as placed on market — total heavy-metal content of each accessible part, per unit mass of that component's material (ug/kg). Not a cosmetic finished-product basis, not a dietary maximum level, and not an EN 71-3 migration/leachate value.
scope_note: Countertop and cordless oral irrigators and water flossers, and the jet tips supplied with them or sold as replacements. These are ARTICLES and no cosmetic finished-product contaminant limit reaches them. The mouth-contact parts (tip, nozzle, and any accessible part of the handle the mouth can reach) take the article-scoped lead ceiling directly. The wetted water path — reservoir, tubing, seals and pump wetted parts — is additionally sampled and held under total-content control on every analyte because it delivers a pressurised jet directly into the oral cavity; no migration ceiling is published for it, because no sovereign sets one for this device form and HMTc does not invent one. Chargers, motor housings and non-wetted, non-mouth-contact electronics are outside the certified article.
basis_guard: ^(?!.*(cosmetic|migration|leachate|colourant|colorant|surface coating|sticker|as consumed|wet weight|candy))(?=.*(content in accessible part|concentration by weight in article))
basis_guard_note: An oral-care article is not a cosmetic and is not a food. The guard admits only article material-content instruments (Canada SOR/2018-83 accessible-part lead content; REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) lead concentration by weight in a mouthable article) and rejects (a) finished-cosmetic impurity limits, which are written for a formulated product and cannot be applied to a polymer filament or a stainless-steel staple, (b) EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48 toy values, which are MIGRATION limits and would understate content by orders of magnitude if read as content, and (c) surface-coating and sticker instruments, which govern an applied film rather than the substrate.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default), Category 20 Oral Care: a formulated oral product takes the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant maximum in its as-sold basis, with the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier read across to non-toothpaste oral-mucosal forms where it is stricter; an oral-care article takes the Canadian mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling and is otherwise held under component-level control. Species never replace totals, no ingredient purity specification anchors a finished-product cell, no migration value anchors a content cell, and no cell is occurrence-derived.

Pb.basis: total lead content per accessible part, ug/kg of that component's material (article content basis, not migration)
Pb.label: Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83) reach mouth-contact consumer products, and section 2(1) caps EACH ACCESSIBLE PART of such a product at 90 mg/kg total lead. An oral-care article is a consumer product brought into contact with the user's mouth in the course of normal use, so the Canadian value directly regulates this cell on the article's own content basis. The only other article-scoped sovereign lead CONTENT instrument in the register, REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) as added by Regulation (EU) 2015/628, sets 0.05% lead by weight (500 mg/kg) for articles that may be placed in the mouth by children; it is five and a half times looser and does not bind.
Pb.substantiation: The Canadian ceiling is applied to every accessible part of the finished article, not to a composite of the whole product, because that is how section 2(1) is written; a composite-averaged result would dilute a leaded component against inert bulk and is not accepted. Components tested separately: the jet tip and nozzle, the tip polymer and any metal insert, the handle body, the accessible housing, and every wetted water-path component (reservoir, tubing, seals, pump wetted parts). Wetted water-path components are sampled as distinct components even where they are not mouth-contact parts, because the water they contact is jetted into the oral cavity within seconds. Two allowances written into the cited instruments are deliberately NOT taken: SOR/2018-83 section 2(2)'s conditional essential-characteristic exception, which substitutes a release criterion for the content criterion, and the REACH entry 63(8)(g) brass-alloy derogation at 0.5% lead by weight. Both are machinability and functional-necessity allowances rather than health findings, and HMTc certifies against the content criterion without them. The EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are likewise not used: they are migration limits on a leachate basis, and reading a migration number as a content ceiling is the basis conflation this row's guard exists to prevent.

Cr.rationale: No sovereign sets a total chromium content limit for a mouth-contact oral-care article. Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83), the only instrument scoped to mouth-contact consumer products on a total-content basis, is lead-only — as is the second article-content lead instrument named in this row's own lead cell, REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) as added by Regulation (EU) 2015/628; the EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are MIGRATION limits and are excluded by this row's basis guard, and finished-cosmetic impurity schedules are written for a formulated product and do not reach an article. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control, not declared not-material: chromium is a defining alloying element of the stainless steel used for staples, wires and tips and is present in chrome plating and in Cr(III) pigments; total chromium is a screen for the Cr(VI) reflex below and is not itself protective.
Cr.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-content analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold, with COMPONENT-LEVEL sampling of the finished article (the jet tip and nozzle, the tip polymer and any metal insert, the handle body, the accessible housing, and every wetted water-path component (reservoir, tubing, seals, pump wetted parts)) — each component digested and reported separately, with no composite-averaged result accepted. No numeric ceiling is published; results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule (ALARA against the tightest available context plus supplier corrective action on the identified component).
